formalization.project_name: Countable cellularity of arbitrary products via finite subproducts

mathematical_sources.note: Directly consulted published exposition, PDF SHA256 d44ee8f6faea16261a8f006afd65d8f7fb378c92ab2ea8637ded2b3fd6353e65. Printed pp.174–175 give the delta-system lemma; printed p.176 Theorem 2.2 and Corollary 2.3 are the exact forward finite-subproduct criterion and separable-product corollary. The iff under nonempty factors, continuous-image transport and discrete boundary are companion proofs. These statements do not use MA or CH; nearby conditional results are excluded. Roy gives classical exposition, not a claim of original discovery, and tentatively traces the criterion to Noble–Ulmer (1972), whose original paper is not claimed directly consulted. No novelty, priority or first-formalization claim.
mathematical_sources.title: Is the product of ccc spaces a ccc space?, Publicacions Matematiques 33 (1989), 173–183

mathematical_sources.note: Directly consulted primary research PDF SHA256 6cf2896ace0650065f02deaf7797f60f9b3ea1c2c6372904c0b05ead145a9e89. Introduction and Section 4 establish the research audience in cellularity and productive chain conditions. Proposition 4.1 is stronger (productively CCC); Theorem 4.4 concerns forcing-poset spectra. Neither stronger statement nor its forcing machinery is claimed formalized.
mathematical_sources.title: A characterization of productive cellularity, arXiv:2005.10325v3

related_formalizations.note: Uses Zorn maximality, finite/countable set APIs, actual product topology, finite-cylinder neighborhoods, finite separable products, and Pairwise.countable_of_isOpen_disjoint. Separable implies CCC is existing Mathlib mathematics, explicitly reused; it is not the principal new bridge.

Prior campaign proves product separability with a continuum index bound and its Boolean sharpness. This independent package proves cellularity for arbitrary index types via the finite-subproduct criterion. No prior package is imported, and no prior theorem is claimed new.
